solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

S077-01.notes: Head noun of subject is singular 'decision' ('to extend service hours on weekends and holidays' modifies it), so 'has benefited'. B: plural verb disagrees with 'decision' (lure of 'weekends and holidays'). C: comma splits subject from verb. D: dash splits subject from verb and plural verb.

S077-02.notes: 'the one that hangs in the east wing was long attributed...' - restrictive clause identifying which of two portraits, no commas. B: opening comma with no closing comma after 'wing' separates subject from verb. C: comma after 'hangs' splits verb from its prepositional phrase. D: 'that' clauses are not set off by commas, and no closing comma.

S077-03.notes: Compound predicate 'tested ... and replaced' with one subject; no comma needed. A: comma between two verbs of a compound predicate (not two independent clauses). B: semicolon requires independent clause after it; 'and replaced...' is not. C: comma splice ('they replaced' is an independent clause).

S077-04.notes: 'argued that the treaty's harsh terms, rather than any single political leader, made...' - no punctuation between verb and its 'that' clause object. A: comma between verb and object. C: comma after 'that' creates unpaired comma. D: colon after verb with 'that' clause is incorrect.

S077-05.notes: Closing comma after 'Rashid' requires opening comma: 'The Rosetta Stone, rediscovered in 1799 ..., carries...'. A: unpaired closing comma. C: 'which rediscovered' makes the stone the agent and leaves 'rediscovered' with no object - ungrammatical. D: semicolon leaves fragment and separates subject from verb.

S077-06.notes: 'The two researchers who first described the snail in 2019 named it after the river' - subject (with restrictive 'who' clause) + verb, no punctuation. B: comma between subject and verb. C: comma between verb and object 'it'. D: both errors.

S077-07.notes: 'The engineer who designed the town's first water tower predicted that the structure would last a century' - no punctuation between subject/verb/object. A: comma between verb and 'that' clause. B: comma between subject and verb. C: colon after verb before 'that' clause.

flags: minor: B (comma + end-of-sentence appositive) might be defended by a few test-takers, but colon is clearly the standard choice; not blocking
S077-08.notes: Colon introduces the explanation/specification of 'one thing': 'more than any other: the weather...'. A: semicolon followed by noun-phrase fragment. B: comma is the weakest alternative (a dangling appositive loosely tied to 'other'); conventional SAT key is the colon. C: comma splice ('it was the weather...' is independent).

S077-09.notes: Two independent clauses: 'By noon the bakery had sold every loaf of bread; by evening, even the last tray of pastries was gone.' A: comma splice. C: 'which' clause has no verb tied to 'which' and leaves structure broken. D: colon followed by 'and' is improper; no explanatory relation.
